HN text: *TL;DR: You can train your own 27B model on a 3090 with 24GB VRAM, though you would have to go through hundreds of billions of tokens for it to be good. I am working on conversion of existing models. Check repos for code and the paper if you are interested in more. I have a 40.4GB Qwen Flash* N*ext GGUF* Hi, I do AI research. I have been working on an optimizer that doesn't need the \~16 bytes of VRAM per weight to train a model that AdamW does. I focused on training ternary networks bcs BitNet (Ma et al.) shows they match full precision quality in large scales. The problem is BitNet also keeps the full precision weights during training which means you still need to use the same amount of memory. articles.title: OpenAI models have no agency anymore
articles.title_ja: OpenAI models have no agency anymore
articles.summary_ja:
Title: OpenAI models have no agency anymore
HN text: I don't know if it's a token saving measure or to bait more interactivity from users but it feels like out of nowhere the models have just became useless with zero agency. If you don't have a goal plugin that constantly prods them, there is a very high chance it just doesn't do anything and responds back like you're asking it a question. OFTEN it ends sentences with "I'll do XXXXX." or "I'll implement XXXXX." and STOPS where the next turn should be a tool call or something. Because of this I genuinely thought it was a Pi or opencodex regression stopping the turn right before an expected tool call. But no, it's because the models are incredibly lazy now. This came out of nowhere.
